# A newer focusout re-validates an older timer's stale focus-leave

## Context

Found while measuring #18290, and it is **not** that ticket's cause — the 60-repeat control came back 6/60 against a 7/60 baseline, so this defect is real and separately owned. Filing it on its own rather than folding it into #18290 as partial progress.

The premise is not secondhand: a red-first arm reproduces it deterministically, without waiting on any race.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-04T17:53Z; no equivalent found. Targeted sweep over `focusout` / `focus leave` / `manager/Focus` returns #6128 (history windowId scoping — different concern) and closed prior art #6162 (`maxFocusInOutGap` 10ms → 30ms) and #8621 (FocusManager stability during atomic moves). Neither describes this. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last ~60 minutes: active claims are #18297, #18281, #18296 and Institution #107 — no overlap. Own-assignment sweep: 9 open, none on this surface.

## The Problem

`Neo.manager.Focus#onFocusout` does not deliver a focus-leave immediately. It defers by `maxFocusInOutGap` (50 ms) so that a focusout followed closely by a focusin can be collapsed into a `focusMove` instead. The deferred callback closes over **its own** `opts`, but decides whether to fire by reading **manager-global** state:

```js
onFocusout(opts) {
    me.lastFocusOutDate = new Date();

    me.timeout(me.maxFocusInOutGap).then(() => {
        if (me.lastFocusOutDate > me.lastFocusInDate) {
            me.focusLeave(opts)
        }
    })
}
```

`lastFocusOutDate` is a singleton field. Any later focusout overwrites it. So a **newer** focusout can push the global date past `lastFocusInDate` and thereby satisfy an **older** timer's condition on its behalf — and that older timer then delivers *its own captured `opts`*, raised against a mount that no longer exists.

Failing interleaving, all within one 50 ms window:

| t | event | effect |
|---|---|---|
| 0 ms | focusout **A** | `lastFocusOutDate = t0`; timer A armed for t50 |
| 10 ms | focusin | `lastFocusInDate = t10`; `t10 - t0 < 50` → `focusMove`, which across identical paths correctly delivers nothing |
| 20 ms | focusout **B** (unrelated) | `lastFocusOutDate = t20` |
| 50 ms | **timer A fires** | `t20 > t10` is true → delivers **A's stale `opts`** |

The focusin at t10 should have disarmed timer A, and it does — until an unrelated focusout re-arms it by side effect.

Consumers receive a leave whose `oldPath` and `relatedTarget` describe a previous mount. A consumer that acts on `!data.relatedTarget` — the documented document-blur / Escape dismissal path — cannot distinguish it from a genuine dismissal, because from inside `onFocusLeave` the payload is indistinguishable.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/Focus.mjs:166-176` — `onFocusout`, the deferred delivery described above. The `opts`/global-state split is the defect.
- `src/manager/Focus.mjs:148-157` — `onFocusin` sets `lastFocusInDate` and routes to `focusMove` or `focusEnter` on the same gap. The two methods share the pair of dates as their only coordination.
- `src/manager/Focus.mjs:185-210` — `setComponentFocus` re-resolves `opts.componentPath` through `Neo.getComponent(id)` at delivery time and calls the handler on every component in the path, so one stale delivery reaches an entire ancestor chain, not a single component.
- `src/component/Base.mjs:1353` — `destroy()` sets `me.onFocusLeave = Neo.emptyFn` with the comment *"We do want to prevent delayed calls after a component instance got destroyed."* **The engine already recognises this hazard class** and neutralises it for destroyed instances. An instance that merely unmounts and remounts keeps a live `onFocusLeave`, so that guard never applies — this ticket closes the same hazard one lifecycle rung down.
- This is app-worker code, not main-realm. `focusin`/`focusout` listeners in the main realm observe nothing here.

Consumers reached by a stale delivery today include `form/field/Base.mjs:356`, `form/field/ComboBox.mjs:551`, `form/field/Picker.mjs:295`, `form/field/Text.mjs:1377`, `form/field/Number.mjs:313`, `menu/List.mjs:527`, `calendar/view/EditEventContainer.mjs:263`, `dashboard/dock/interaction/RevealOverlay.mjs:550`, and `table/plugin/CellEditing.mjs:236`.

## The Fix

Gate the deferred callback on **timer identity**, not merely on recency: capture the `Date` this invocation wrote, and deliver only if it is still the one the manager holds.

```js
onFocusout(opts) {
    let me   = this,
        date = new Date();

    me.lastFocusOutDate = date;

    me.timeout(me.maxFocusInOutGap).then(() => {
        if (me.lastFocusOutDate === date && date > me.lastFocusInDate) {
            me.focusLeave(opts)
        }
    })
}
```

One added binding and one added conjunct. `date > me.lastFocusInDate` preserves the existing null-`lastFocusInDate` behaviour exactly (both sides coerce identically). A superseded focusout stands down; the newest one still delivers its own `opts` through its own timer.

Deliberately **not** touched: `menu/List.mjs#onFocusLeave`'s predicate. Its `!data.relatedTarget` branch is the documented document-blur/Escape dismissal path and is covered by an arm; weakening it trades a stale delivery for a menu that will not close. The ordering is not knowable at the consumer, which is why the fix belongs here.

| `Neo.manager.Focus#onFocusout` (`src/manager/Focus.mjs:166`) | this ticket | only the most recent focusout may deliver its deferred leave | a superseded focusout stands down silently; the newest still delivers | JSDoc in place | red-first unit arm, both directions |
| `Neo.manager.Focus#maxFocusInOutGap` (`:39`, default `50`) | existing config | unchanged; still the collapse window | tuning it does not change delivery identity | existing | arm reads the config rather than hard-coding 50 |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this repairs delivery within an accepted primitive; no ADR authority is amended, challenged, or depended upon.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A red-first unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs` delivers focusout → focusin → a second, unrelated focusout, and asserts the first focusout's components receive **no** leave. It must fail before the fix and pass after.
- [ ] The same arm asserts the **later** focusout still delivers its own leave. Without this half the arm passes if `focusLeave` never runs at all, which is a different bug.
- [ ] The arm derives its waits from `FocusManager.maxFocusInOutGap` rather than hard-coding `50`, so a future change to that config cannot silently make the arm vacuous.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` is green across the full suite — every consumer listed under Architectural Reality is covered by existing arms, and this is the blast-radius check.
- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/menu/List.spec.mjs` — *"keeps document blur and Escape as immediate dismissal paths"* (`:173`) and *"treats the trigger and every mounted submenu level as inside, but dismisses outside"* (`:103`) both still pass unmodified.
- [ ] `test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs:119` — *"a leaf click takes every level down together"* still passes unmodified.
- [ ] No consumer file is modified. The diff is `src/manager/Focus.mjs` plus its spec.

## Out of Scope

- **#18290.** This is not its fix: measured 6/60 against a 7/60 baseline. That ticket stays open with its own cause unfound.
- Changing `maxFocusInOutGap`, or the focusout→focusin→`focusMove` collapse policy itself. `#6162` already moved that value once; this ticket does not revisit it.
- `setComponentFocus`'s re-resolution of ids through `Neo.getComponent` at delivery time. It is correct for a live instance under the same id, and with delivery identity fixed it has no observed defect. Noted, not addressed.
- Windowed scoping of `history` — that is #6128.

## Avoided Traps

- **Treating this as a menu bug.** The symptom was first seen through `menu.List`, and the consumer-side guard is the obvious place to reach for. It was measured and eliminated: a mount-generation guard in the consumer scored 7/60 with and 7/60 without, because the leave never carried a generation to key on. The ordering is not the consumer's to know.
- **Reading the same failure count as the same failure.** This ticket exists precisely because a real, red-first-proven mechanism turned out not to move the symptom it was found under. A mechanism arm going green is evidence about the mechanism, never about a symptom.
- **Comparing dates instead of identity.** `lastFocusOutDate > lastFocusInDate` reads like a freshness check and is one — for the *manager*, not for *this* timer. Any fix that keeps comparing only timestamps reproduces the defect the moment a third event lands in the window.
